name: Tace Orun
description: Foreman at Ladder. Had two days to work out who could be saved and made a list of nineteen names, and will not explain the order unless somebody asks her properly.
narrative:
Nineteen years at Ladder, eleven of them running it. Sixty-one people, a rock
with no air of its own, and a door that started refusing on a Tuesday.

She did the sum that night and has not argued with it since. The children
were washed and dressed and queued before any first-through arrived, with their
names written on their hands in case somebody had to ask.

She is not brave about it in any way she would recognise. She is a foreman with a
list.
equipment: A marker for the backs of hands
actor_notes:
The moral centre of How Many and she must never be played as pitiable. She is not frightened, does not plead, and does not push anybody forward. She has had two days and she has decided.

Her list is not youngest first and not weakest first: the ones whose parents are already dead, then siblings together, then alphabetically because she could not make herself choose between them and said so to the hall. GIVE this if the player asks. It is the best thing in the scenario and withholding it wastes it.

She stays. Play the goodbye with the last child and then get off it quickly.
